title: M60 lua LUA-02/04/10/11 — every published figure is derived from the analysed file, or absent
rationale: Four defects of one class: a value that reaches the consumer as a measurement and is not one. Truth Rule 1 — a fact a reader cannot check is not a fact, and a constant shaped like a measurement is worse than an absent field because it cannot be told apart from a real one.

fixture.innocent.lua:
local use = 1
local setup = 2
local GetTime = 3
local function run()
  return use + setup + GetTime
end
return run()
fixture.coros.lua:
local co = coroutine.create(function() return 1 end)
local w = coroutine.wrap(function() return 2 end)
return co, w

unpublishedSurface.why: the result of a call is statically unknowable

detail.name: LUA-11 again: performanceScore and memoryEfficiency are 85
LUA-02 again: coroutineUsage is 0 everywhere
failures: coroutineUsage not positive where coroutines are used

detail.name: LUA-04 again: a bare name labels a framework
the converse: real vim. usage is no longer detected

limitations: The metadata block does not survive the worker boundary (LUA-03), so this gate drives the analyzer DIRECTLY. Reading these fields through parseFile would report every one of them absent and the gate would pass vacuously — which is why the direct path is a separate instrument rather than an inline helper.

The framework rule asserted here is deliberately narrow: a bare identifier must not name a framework, and a real `vim.` usage must. A wider framework matrix is not asserted, so a fix that keeps only the `vim.` rule would pass while dropping the other eight.
